en.title: Why Delta's brand-new Airbus A321neos sat in the desert while flying 44 recliners instead
en.summary: Certification delays for the Safran Vue business class seat left several of Delta's newly delivered Airbus A321neos parked in desert storage; the airline's workaround is an interim cabin with 44 domestic first class recliners instead of lie-flat suites.
body: When airlines order a new fleet, the assumption is straightforward: aircraft arrive from the manufacturer, crews are trained, routes are assigned and passengers start flying soon afterwards. Delta Air Lines' newest Airbus A321neos became an unusual exception, as a single component disrupted an entire fleet strategy, leaving several factory-fresh narrowbodies sitting in desert storage for months.

At the centre of the strategy was the Safran Vue business class seat, a reverse-herringbone design that positioned passengers toward the window. The planned cabin featured 16 lie-flat business class suites, 12 premium economy seats, 54 Comfort+ seats and 66 economy seats for premium transcontinental routes such as New York JFK to Los Angeles. But reports throughout 2025 and 2026 pointed to persistent certification challenges, with the US Federal Aviation Administration's human factors testing and crashworthiness requirements keeping the seat from entering commercial service.

Delta had already accepted delivery of several A321neos during 2024, yet without certified seats the aircraft could not enter service as intended. The airline eventually opted for a practical workaround, introducing an interim cabin in May with 44 domestic first class recliner seats, alongside 54 Comfort+ and 66 economy seats. The temporary layout lets the aircraft fly and earn revenue, though 44 premium passengers share a single forward lavatory, and reports suggest Delta may abandon the Safran Vue altogether for the Thompson Vantage Solo seat already used by JetBlue and American Airlines.

zh.title: 達美全新A321neo為何在沙漠停放：Safran Vue座椅認證卡關、改飛44個頭等躺椅
zh.summary: 達美航空全新A321neo原定搭載Safran Vue平躺商務艙套房，卻因座椅認證延宕，多架新機在2024年交付後只能停放沙漠；達美改以44個國內頭等艙躺椅臨時上陣，讓飛機先行載客。
body: 航空公司訂購新機隊時，通常假設飛機自製造商交付、機組完成訓練、航線分配後便能很快載客。然而達美航空最新的空中巴士A321neo卻成為例外：一個零件的認證延宕打亂了整個機隊策略，多架全新窄體客機在沙漠停放數月，等待航空公司找到讓它們投入營運的方法。
問題核心是Safran Vue商務艙座椅。這款反魚骨式座椅讓乘客面向窗戶，原定搭載於達美A321neo的頂級跨洲航線，客艙規劃為16個平躺商務艙套房、12個豪華經濟艙座位、54個優悅經濟艙座位與66個經濟艙座位。但座椅認證在2025年與2026年間持續遇到挑戰，美國聯邦航空總署的人因測試與耐撞性要求，使座椅遲遲無法獲准進入商業服務。

達美已在2024年間接收數架A321neo，卻因座椅未獲認證而無法以上述形式投入服務。與其無限期等待，達美最終選擇務實的權宜方案：5月推出臨時客艙，改裝44個國內頭等艙躺椅座位，搭配54個優悅經濟艙座位與66個經濟艙座位，讓飛機先行載客、創造營收。不過44名前艙乘客僅共用1間前方洗手間，長程跨洲航線可能出現排隊；報導也指出，達美可能放棄Safran Vue，改採已獲多家航空公司使用的Thompson Vantage Solo座椅。

facts.claim: Delta's A321neo premium transcontinental cabin was planned with 16 lie-flat business class suites, 12 premium economy seats, 54 Comfort+ seats and 66 economy seats.
The Safran Vue seat uses a reverse-herringbone design positioning passengers toward the window.
Reports throughout 2025 and 2026 pointed to persistent certification challenges for the Safran Vue involving FAA human factors testing and crashworthiness requirements.
Delta accepted delivery of several A321neos during 2024, but the aircraft sat in desert storage without certified seats.
The interim cabin introduced in May has 44 domestic first class recliner seats, 54 Comfort+ seats and 66 economy seats.
Reports suggest Delta may abandon the Safran Vue for the Thompson Vantage Solo seat, already used by JetBlue and American Airlines.
